ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Experts believe that the Earth should also, like the Moon, have once suffered many meteorite impacts, but at present obvious meteorite craters are rarely found on the land surface. What is the main reason for this?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Experts believe that the Earth should also, like the Moon, have once suffered many meteorite impacts, but at present obvious meteorite craters are rarely found on the land surface. What is the main reason for this?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left side of the image is labeled “Earth”; the Earth can be seen as spherical, with obvious cloud systems on the surface and unevenly bright and dark sea-land features; the right side is labeled “Moon”; in the picture the lunar surface is relatively gray and dark, the overall sense of pits and hollows is more obvious, and it is accompanied by a probe image. Then reason: the question stem says that both the Earth and the Moon have once suffered many meteorite impacts, but now obvious meteorite craters are rarely found on the Earth's land surface. This shows that the difference is not that the Earth was not impacted, but whether the impact craters were preserved for a long time after forming. The Earth's surface is continuously modified by internal and external geological processes such as weathering, erosion, transport, deposition, tectonic movement, and volcanic activity; meteorite craters will be destroyed, buried, or have their forms changed; while the Moon's geological activity is weak, and meteorite craters are more easily preserved. Therefore the main reason is modification by geological processes.
